predecessors.name: Maya city-states (Preclassic and Classic)
predecessors.text: Tikal and its immediate land (the city covers more than 16 km2; earthworks enclose about 120 km2)

successors.name: Maya city-states (Postclassic)
successors.text: Tikal's core territory, 'at least 25 kilometers in every direction', with Uaxactun absorbed

ledger.x: About 50: the Tikal dynasty is founded.
331: Caracol, founded this year, begins as a client of Tikal.
About 450: Tikal's core grows to 25 km and more in every direction.
562: Calakmul and Caracol defeat Tikal and Caracol leaves Tikal's orbit.

wars.name: Intervention of Teotihuacan at Tikal
wars.outcome: On 14 January 378 Siyaj K'ak' arrived and the Tikal king Chak Tok Ich'aak died; no territory is recorded as changing hands.

wars.name: Tikal-Caracol axe war
wars.outcome: Tikal 'enacted a ch'ak (axe) war and defeated Caracol' in 556; Caracol took revenge in 562.

wars.name: Calakmul-Caracol defeat of Tikal
wars.outcome: Tikal was defeated and its king sacrificed in 562 ('Sky Witness defeated Tikal itself and sacrificed its king'); Caracol left Tikal's orbit and a 130-year hiatus began.

wars.name: Tikal-Dos Pilas war
wars.outcome: Tikal captured Dos Pilas in 672 and held it, driving the king into exile, until 677; in 679 Dos Pilas defeated Tikal.

wars.name: Tikal-Calakmul battle of 695
wars.outcome: In August 695 Jasaw Chan K'awiil I defeated Calakmul in 'a catastrophic battle'; Tikal 'was able to turn the tables on its great rival'.

certainty.note: Classic Maya kingdoms had no fixed borders; the core radii are the grid's minimum, not measured frontiers.
